what_it_does: Processing-in-memory (doing arithmetic inside or very close to the memory chip rather than sending data across a long wire to a separate processor) is a promising way to reduce the enormous cost of moving data around AI accelerators. When multiple such memory-compute units are connected into a network on a chip (a grid of wires and switches that routes data between units), the best arrangement of those connections depends on which units are doing what kind of work. Existing tools for finding a good network layout assume all units are identical, which breaks down when units have different capabilities. HPIM-NoC is a framework that can simulate and then search for the best network layout for these mixed, heterogeneous systems, using a guided search algorithm (simulated annealing — a technique that explores many options while gradually narrowing in on a good one) and tricks to run the search quickly.
